title: Optimal Lower Bounds for Online Multicalibration

We show that any “proper” black-box reduction from marginal calibration to multicalibration must itself incur multicalibration error Ω ​ ( T 1 − γ ) \Omega(T^{1-\gamma}) for any constant γ > 0 \gamma>0 unless it uses exponentially many oracle copies. Our construction uses a binary group family of cardinality | G | = Θ ​ ( log ⁡ T ) |G|=\Theta(\log T) , and so serves as an obstruction to a reductions-based strategy to giving o ​ ( T 2 / 3 ) o(T^{2/3}) upper bounds for multicalibration in this regime. We define the notion of a “context-blind” oracle: A (possibly randomized) forecasting algorithm A A is context-blind if for every round t t its output distribution depends only on its internal state (i.e. on its own past transcript) and not on the current context x t x^{t} . Equivalently, for any realized internal randomness of A A , the mapping x t ↦ Q t x^{t}\mapsto Q^{t} produced by A A on round t t is constant. If A A is any algorithm with a worst-case marginal calibration guarantee that holds for all context sequences, then feeding A A a fixed dummy context x ¯ \bar{x} on every round (and otherwise running it unchanged) produces a context-blind algorithm with the same marginal guarantee.
